mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly FEDFUNDS rate above the prior 12-month average predicts a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return as higher policy rates discount future equity cash flows.
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when FEDFUNDS crosses the threshold (Granger causality p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4%, labor market slack increases, boosting consumer confidence and driving positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: In regimes where unemployment is <4%, the 60-day forward return is not significantly higher than the 4% threshold (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising HOUST (household spending) above 2% MoM suggest accelerating demand, which is associated with positive S&P 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 100 instances where HOUST crosses the 2% threshold but 20-day forward returns are negative (Rank IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO (industrial production) index below 95 triggers a supply-side shock that produces negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: More than 30% of INDPRO < 95 events do not precede negative 20-day forward returns (Granger causality p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in both FEDFUNDS and GDPC1 (gDP momentum) over the prior quarter predict a 5-day negative S&P 5-day forward return as tightening and weak momentum reinforce each other.
failure_condition: In 100 such events, 5-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When PAYEMS (employment) rises by more than 10,000 in a month, it indicates labor market strength and is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: Over 200 trigger events, 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in CPIAUCSL (inflation) below 0.2% for three consecutive months is interpreted as disinflation and predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: In 500 such windows, 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (Granger causality p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales) falls by more than 5% in a month, it signals weak consumer demand and is associated with negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: More than 80 such events do not precede negative 20-day forward returns (p > 0.1).
